model: segmentation-models-pytorch UNet++ (ResNet34 ImageNet encoder, full-res decoder), 1-ch input, pointwise log norm, focal x10 + dice; best val checkpoint (step 5000) of run smp_upp34_a; threshold 0.99 picked on val
based_on: smp_unet UnetPlusPlus (h7 run smp_upp34_a, best.pt step 5000)

train.command: python -m seg.train --model smp_unet --config configs/smp_unet.yaml --out $PK/runs/h7/smp_upp34_a --time-min 90 --set model.arch=UnetPlusPlus --set train.num_workers=5 --set train.seed=1 --set train.max_steps=25000

notes: Interim update (replaces the 0.9061 smp Unet r34 snapshot). Single model, no TTA, no post-processing: smp UNet++ r34 best val checkpoint (step 5000 of 10469; in-training val F1 0.9285 on 150 val imgs at thr 0.9). Threshold re-picked by seg.evaluate on every 3rd val image (488 imgs) over 0.5..0.995 -> 0.99 (val F1 0.922), then the whole test split (1529 images). Earlier: smp Unet r34 snapshot test F1 0.9061. Findings: full-res decoders matter for 1-2 px peaks; FPs are confident 1-2 px spots far from labeled peaks that look like real unlabeled peaks (precision ceiling ~0.9 from the labels); min-size/closing post-processing did not help; flip TTA +0.002 on val; saturated-pixel masking no effect for this model. Next: val-selected ensemble (r34 last + UNet++ best, flip TTA) running.
